subtopics.notes:
### Regulators — who watches which market
- **SEBI** — securities market regulator; set up 1988 (executive), statutory by the **SEBI Act, 1992** (after the Harshad Mehta episode); HQ **Mumbai**.
- **IRDAI** — insurance regulator under the **IRDA Act, 1999**; HQ **Hyderabad**.
- **PFRDA** — pension regulator (interim 2003; statutory by the **PFRDA Act, 2013**); runs **NPS** and **APY**; HQ New Delhi.
- **RBI** — banks, NBFCs, payment systems. Others worth a line: **NABARD** (rural credit apex), **SIDBI** (small-industry finance), real-estate **RERA** (2016).

### Development finance institutions
- **NABARD** — **12 July 1982**, on the **Shivaraman committee's** advice, taking over RBI's agricultural-refinance functions; apex for rural credit, refinances RRBs and co-operative banks; HQ Mumbai; owned by the Government of India.
- **SIDBI** — **1990**, HQ **Lucknow**; refinance window for small industries and the fund manager for MUDRA.
- **EXIM Bank** — **1982**, trade finance; **NHB** — **1988**, housing finance regulator-turned-developer of the housing market.

### Markets and exchanges
The **BSE (1875)** — Asia's oldest exchange, began as the Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association — publishes the **Sensex (30 stocks)**. The **NSE** (incorporated 1992, trading from 1994) brought screen-based trading and publishes the **Nifty 50**. **NPCI (2008)**, the payments umbrella body, built **UPI (2016), RuPay, IMPS, FASTag**. Shares are held electronically with two depositories — **NSDL and CDSL** — while the **FSDC** (Financial Stability and Development Council, 2010) coordinates regulators at the apex level, chaired by the Union Finance Minister.

### Multilateral institutions — HQs to memorise
| Institution | Year | HQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| IMF | 1944 (Bretton Woods) | Washington DC | quotas, SDRs, BoP support |
| World Bank | 1944 | Washington DC | IBRD + IDA |
| WTO | **1995** (GATT 1947/48 before) | **Geneva** | 164 members, trade rules |
| **ADB** | **1966** | **Manila** | regional development bank |
| **AIIB** | **2016** | **Beijing** | India an early, large shareholder |
| **New Development Bank** | **2015** | **Shanghai** | BRICS bank; first president K.V. Kamath |
| FATF | 1989 | Paris | money-laundering watchdog (India member since 2010) |

### Quick revision
- SEBI 1992 Act, Mumbai; IRDAI 1999, Hyderabad; PFRDA 2013 Act, New Delhi (NPS).
- NABARD 12-7-1982 (Shivaraman; from RBI agri refinance); SIDBI 1990 Lucknow; EXIM 1982; NHB 1988.
- BSE 1875 (Asia's oldest) → Sensex 30; NSE 1992/94 → Nifty 50; NPCI 2008 → UPI 2016.
- IMF/WB 1944 Washington; WTO 1995 Geneva; ADB 1966 Manila; AIIB 2016 Beijing; NDB 2015 Shanghai (BRICS); FATF Paris.

patterns.name: Regulator ↔ sector matching
patterns.howToSpot: 'SEBI regulates', 'the insurance regulator is', 'who runs the NPS', matching each regulator with its market.
patterns.logic:
1. One line each: **SEBI** — securities; **IRDAI** — insurance; **PFRDA** — pensions (NPS/APY); **RBI** — banks, NBFCs, payments.
2. Year hooks: SEBI statutory **1992**; IRDAI **1999**; PFRDA statutory **2013** (interim 2003).
3. If the question names 'stock broker' or 'mutual fund', the answer is SEBI; 'policy-holder' points to IRDAI.

example.q: The regulation of the **securities market** in India vests in —
example.solution: **SEBI**, constituted in 1988 and made statutory by the SEBI Act, **1992**; headquartered in Mumbai.

patterns.name: Institution ↔ headquarters
patterns.howToSpot: 'SIDBI is headquartered at', 'the IRDAI sits in', matching development banks and regulators with cities.
patterns.logic:
1. Financial-sector HQs: **SIDBI — Lucknow** (the classic answer); **IRDAI — Hyderabad**; SEBI, NABARD, EXIM — Mumbai; NHB and PFRDA — New Delhi.
2. Multilaterals: IMF/World Bank — Washington; **ADB — Manila**; **AIIB — Beijing**; **NDB — Shanghai**; WTO — Geneva; FATF — Paris.
3. Lucknow and Hyderabad are the two 'surprise' HQs exams love.

example.q: The **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** is headquartered in —
example.solution: **Lucknow** — set up in **1990** as the apex refinancer for small industries (and MUDRA's fund manager).

patterns.name: Year ↔ founding event
patterns.howToSpot: 'NABARD was established in', 'Asia's oldest stock exchange is', matching years with institutions.
patterns.logic:
1. India: BSE **1875** (Asia's oldest); NSE 1992/1994; NPCI 2008; NABARD **1982**; SIDBI 1990; EXIM 1982; NHB 1988.
2. Multilaterals: IMF/WB **1944** (Bretton Woods); WTO **1995** (GATT 1947 before); ADB 1966; NDB 2015; AIIB 2016.
3. 'Oldest exchange in Asia' = **BSE**, born as the Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association.

example.q: Which is **Asia's oldest stock exchange**?
example.solution: The **BSE, Bombay (1875)** — founded as the Native Share & Stock Brokers' Association; the NSE followed only in 1992.

patterns.name: Multilateral banks and funds
patterns.howToSpot: 'The New Development Bank is headquartered at', 'which bank do BRICS countries own', 'the ADB was set up in', matching multilaterals with HQ and membership.
patterns.logic:
1. **NDB (2015, Shanghai)** = the **BRICS** bank; first president **K.V. Kamath**.
2. **AIIB (2016, Beijing)** — India an early member and second-largest shareholder.
3. IMF = balance-of-payments support, quotas and **SDRs**; World Bank = long-term development lending; both born at **Bretton Woods, 1944**.

example.q: The **New Development Bank**, set up by BRICS nations in 2015, is headquartered in —
example.solution: **Shanghai** — with **K.V. Kamath** as its first president; it funds infrastructure and sustainable development.

patterns.name: Indices, exchanges and payment rails
patterns.howToSpot: 'The Sensex comprises', 'Nifty belongs to which exchange', 'UPI is operated by', matching index ↔ exchange and product ↔ operator.
patterns.logic:
1. **Sensex — 30 stocks, BSE**; **Nifty 50 — NSE**; both free-float market-cap weighted.
2. **NPCI (2008)** operates **UPI, RuPay, IMPS, FASTag, NACH**; UPI went live in **2016**.
3. Depositories: **NSDL and CDSL** hold shares electronically — a frequent fourth option in such questions.

example.q: **UPI** is built and operated by —
example.solution: **NPCI** (National Payments Corporation of India, est. **2008**) — the umbrella body behind UPI (live 2016), RuPay, IMPS and FASTag.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Policy rates and the monetary corridor
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The repo rate is the rate at which', 'the SDF sits how far below the repo', 'who holds the casting vote in the MPC', or a table of rate ↔ definition is offered.
pyqPatterns.approach: Fix the corridor's geometry, not its numbers: SDF = repo − 25 bp (floor, collateral-free), MSF = Bank Rate = repo + 25 bp (ceiling). MPC = 6 members (3 RBI, Governor casting vote), bi-monthly, CPI 4% ± 2%, breach reported after 3 quarters. CRR is cash with the RBI; SLR is the bank's own liquid assets — never call them policy rates.

example.q: In India's current framework, the **Bank Rate** equals —
example.solution: The **MSF rate** — repo + 25 basis points at the corridor ceiling; the SDF (repo − 25 bp) is the floor.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The WPI is compiled by', 'which index does the RBI target', 'the new GDP series uses which base year' — options pair CPI, WPI, IIP, deflator with agencies and bases.
pyqPatterns.approach: Grid it: CPI — NSO/MoSPI, retail, services included, new base 2024 (Feb 2026); WPI — Office of Economic Adviser (DPIIT), wholesale, goods only, new base 2022-23 (Jun 2026) with PPIs; IIP — NSO output index, re-based 2022-23; CPI-IW — Labour Bureau (DA linkage). RBI targets headline CPI, never WPI.

example.q:
Which pair is correctly matched?
(a) WPI — NSO (b) CPI — Office of Economic Adviser (c) IIP — a price index (d) CPI-IW — Labour Bureau
example.solution: (d) — CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau and drives dearness allowance. WPI belongs to DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser, CPI to the NSO, and the IIP measures output, not prices.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'The Mahalanobis model belongs to which plan', 'growth with stability was the objective of', ordering of plans or spotting the last plan and the plan interludes.
pyqPatterns.approach: Two model pairs carry the marks: 1st — Harrod-Domar (agriculture), 2nd — Mahalanobis (heavy industry). Theme hooks: 4th growth with stability, 8th launched with the 1991 LPG reforms, 11th inclusive, 12th (2012-17) the last plan. Interludes: Plan Holiday 1966-69, Rolling Plan 1978-80, annual plans 1990-92.

example.q: The **Harrod-Domar model** formed the basis of which Five Year Plan?
example.solution: The **First Plan (1951-56)** — agriculture and irrigation priority; the 2nd plan switched to Mahalanobis and heavy industry.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Budget structure, funds and deficit arithmetic
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Either figures for expenditure, receipts and interest are given and a deficit is asked, or articles/funds are matched: Annual Financial Statement 112, Consolidated Fund 266(1), Contingency Fund 267.
pyqPatterns.approach: Four formulas settle it: RD = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts; ERD = RD − capital-asset grants; FD = total expenditure − receipts excluding borrowings; PD = FD − interest (can be negative). Articles: 112 AFS, 266 two funds, 267 Contingency (President, ₹30,000 crore). Budget on 1 February since 2017; Railway Budget merged 2017; Economic Survey the day before.

example.q: Total expenditure ₹45 lakh crore, receipts excluding borrowings ₹39 lakh crore, interest payments ₹10 lakh crore. The primary deficit is —
example.solution: 6 − 10 = **−₹4 lakh crore** — a primary surplus: FD = 45 − 39 = 6, then subtract interest.

pyqPatterns.pattern: GST: articles, council and the slab reform
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Article 279A provides for', 'GST was introduced from', 'the new slabs after the 2025 reform are' — plus CGST/SGST/IGST structure and council voting shares.
pyqPatterns.approach: Chain: 101st Amendment (2016) → GST from 1 July 2017 → Articles 246A (power), 269A (IGST), 279A (Council). Council: Union FM chairs, 3/4 weighted majority, Centre 1/3 vs states 2/3. Slabs since 22 September 2025 (Council decision 3 September 2025): 5% merit and 18% standard, 40% demerit rate, 12% abolished.

example.q: In the GST Council, the combined weighted vote share of the **states** is —
example.solution: **Two-thirds** — the Centre holds one-third and decisions need a three-fourths majority, so states together can block but not pass.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: '₹6,000 a year is given under', 'Har Ghar Jal is the goal of', 'which ministry runs POSHAN', or match-the-column pairing schemes with years and benefits.
pyqPatterns.approach: Anchor on the rupee figures and dates: PM-KISAN ₹6,000/yr (2019); PM-JAY ₹5 lakh/family (2018); MUDRA tiers 50k/5L/10L (2015); Jan Dhan 28-8-2014; SBM 2-10-2014; Ujjwala 1-5-2016; JJM 2019; Gati Shakti 2021. Employment: MGNREGA (100 days) replaced by VB-G RAM G from 1 July 2026 — 125 days, weekly wages.

example.q: The health cover of **₹5 lakh per family per year** for hospitalisation is provided under —
example.solution: **Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY** (23 September 2018); its digital arm, the ABDM (2021), issues ABHA health IDs.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Regulators, institutions and multilaterals: sector, HQ, year
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'SEBI became statutory in', 'SIDBI is headquartered at', 'the NDB of BRICS is based in', pairs mixing regulators, development banks and multilateral institutions.
pyqPatterns.approach: Sector lines: SEBI — securities (1992 Act, Mumbai); IRDAI — insurance (1999, Hyderabad); PFRDA — pensions (2013 Act, New Delhi); RBI — banks and payments. Dev banks: NABARD 1982 (Mumbai), SIDBI 1990 (**Lucknow**), EXIM 1982, NHB 1988. Multilaterals: IMF/WB 1944 Washington, WTO 1995 Geneva, ADB 1966 Manila, AIIB 2016 Beijing, NDB 2015 Shanghai.

example.q:
Which pair is correctly matched?
(a) IRDAI — Mumbai (b) SIDBI — Lucknow (c) ADB — Beijing (d) NDB — Manila
example.solution: (b) — SIDBI (1990) is headquartered at Lucknow. IRDAI sits at Hyderabad, the ADB at Manila, and the BRICS NDB at Shanghai.

pyqPatterns.pattern: Statement-based economy (2-3 statements, pick correct set)
pyqPatterns.howToSpot: Numbered statements about monetary policy, the budget, GST or a flagship scheme are offered and the candidate picks which are correct — the dominant PYQ format for this topic.
pyqPatterns.approach: Hunt the planted error first: 'payment banks can lend' (false), 'the RBI targets WPI' (false — CPI), 'fiscal deficit never exceeds revenue deficit' (false), 'cesses are shared with states' (false — outside the divisible pool), 'Plan Holiday followed the 2nd plan' (false — the 3rd). If one statement is clearly wrong, three options fall at once.

example.q: Consider: 1. The MPC has six members. 2. The RBI's inflation target is framed on the WPI. 3. Payment banks cannot undertake lending. Which are correct?
example.solution: Statements 1 and 3 only — the MPC has six members with the Governor's casting vote, the target is **CPI** 4% ± 2%, and payment banks take deposits without lending.

solvedExamples.q: If the nominal GDP of India is ₹300 lakh crore and the GDP deflator is 125, the real GDP (base-year prices) is:
solvedExamples.solution: GDP deflator = (Nominal ÷ Real) × 100, so Real = Nominal ÷ 1.25 = 300 ÷ 1.25 = **₹240 lakh crore**. Option (b) uses a wrong 133 deflator intuition; (c) multiplies instead of divides; (d) is a pure guess close to 240.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Deflator above 100 → divide nominal by (deflator/100) to get real.

solvedExamples.q: As per the RBI monetary policy of August 2026, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: The SDF is 25 basis points below the repo rate
The MSF is 25 basis points below the repo rate
The Bank Rate is 40 basis points below the repo rate
The CRR stands at 4 per cent
solvedExamples.solution: Repo 5.25% → **SDF 5.00% (repo − 25 bp)**; MSF and Bank Rate are 5.50% (repo **+** 25 bp); CRR is **3%** (cut from 4% during Sep–Nov 2025). The corridor is SDF 5.00% — repo 5.25% — MSF 5.50%.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Corridor memory hook: SDF = repo minus a quarter, MSF = repo plus a quarter.

solvedExamples.q: From Budget 2026-27 figures — revenue receipts ₹35.3 lakh crore, revenue expenditure ₹41.3 lakh crore and interest payments ₹14.0 lakh crore — the revenue deficit is:
solvedExamples.solution: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts = 41.3 − 35.3 = **₹6.0 lakh crore** (actual RE figure ≈ ₹5.9 lakh crore, 1.5% of GDP). Option (a) is the primary deficit (16.9 − 14.0), (c) is the fiscal deficit, (d) is the previous year's RE.
solvedExamples.shortcut: First classify each number as revenue or fiscal — only revenue items enter revenue deficit.

solvedExamples.q: Under GST 2.0 (effective 22 September 2025), small cars and air-conditioners attract GST at:
solvedExamples.solution: The 56th GST Council's rationalisation moved most 28%-slab items — small cars, ACs, large TVs — to **18%**, while sin/luxury goods (pan masala, aerated drinks, luxury cars) went to the new **40%** demerit slab. The 12% slab was abolished altogether.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Ask 'sin or comfort?' — comfort items slid to 18%, sin items jumped to 40%.

practice.q: The Second Five Year Plan of India was based on which model of economic development?
practice.solution: The **2nd Plan (1956-61)** followed the **P.C. Mahalanobis model**, prioritising heavy and capital-goods industries. The 1st Plan leaned on the Harrod-Domar framework with an agriculture focus; the wage-goods critique came from Vakil-Brahmanand.
practice.shortcut: Second plan = heavy industry = Mahalanobis (the 'big machines' man).

practice.q: In which year were 14 major commercial banks nationalised in India?
practice.solution: **19 July 1969** — banks with deposits over ₹50 crore were nationalised; six more followed in April 1980 (₹200 crore threshold). SBI's creation from the Imperial Bank was in 1955, and the RBI itself was nationalised in 1949.

practice.q: With reference to NITI Aayog, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It was set up in 2014 as the successor to the Finance Commission
It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament
It continues the Five Year Plan process
It was established on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission
practice.solution: NITI Aayog was created by a **Cabinet resolution on 1 January 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission (1950) after the 12th Plan ended. It is neither constitutional nor statutory, and it does not allocate Plan funds.
practice.shortcut: Statutory test fails → only the '1 Jan 2015 replacement' statement can be true.

practice.q: The GST 2.0 rate rationalisation — with 5% and 18% slabs and a 40% demerit rate — took effect from:
practice.solution: The 56th GST Council **decided** the restructuring on 3 September 2025, but the new rates were **effective 22 September 2025** (first day of Navratri). 1 July 2017 is GST's launch date; 1 April 2026 is the Income-tax Act, 2025 date.
practice.shortcut: Decision 3 Sep, effect 22 Sep — decision first, delivery on Navratri.

practice.q: As per the RBI's monetary policy statement of August 2026, the policy (repo) rate stands at:
practice.solution: The MPC (5 Aug 2026) **unanimously held the repo at 5.25%** with a neutral stance — the rate last moved down through the 2025 easing cycle. 5.00% is the SDF floor and 5.50% the MSF/bank rate ceiling.
practice.shortcut: Remember the corridor trio 5.00–5.25–5.50; repo sits in the middle.

practice.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is budgeted at what percentage of GDP?
practice.solution: **4.3% of GDP (BE 2026-27)**, improving on the 4.4% Revised Estimate of 2025-26; total expenditure is ₹53.47 lakh crore. The debt-to-GDP path heads from 55.6% toward about 50% by March 2031.

practice.q: The new series of the Consumer Price Index released in February 2026 uses which base year?
practice.solution: MoSPI's new CPI series (from 12 Feb 2026) shifts the base from **2012 to 2024**. 2022-23 is the new base for **GDP and IIP**, and the WPI moved to 2022-23 in June 2026.
practice.shortcut: Consumer prices anchor on a calendar year (2024); production series take financial years (2022-23).

practice.q: Which of the following constitutes M1 (narrow money) in India?
options: Currency with the public + time deposits with banks
Currency with the public + demand deposits with banks + other deposits with the RBI
Currency with the public + post office savings deposits
practice.solution: **M1 = currency with the public + demand (current/savings) deposits with banks + 'other deposits' with the RBI.** Time deposits enter only M2/M3; post-office deposits sit outside M1, and M3 = M1 + time deposits (broad money).
practice.shortcut: Narrow = instantly spendable — currency plus demand deposits only.

practice.q: The Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, guarantees:
options: 100 days of employment per household, as under MGNREGA
125 days of wage employment per rural household per year, effective 1 July 2026
practice.solution: The VB-G RAM G Act (2025) raises the statutory guarantee from 100 to **125 days** per rural household per financial year and came into force on **1 July 2026**, with weekly wage payments replacing the 15-day cycle.

practice.q: If a government's fiscal deficit is ₹12,00,000 crore and its interest payments are ₹9,00,000 crore, its primary deficit is:
practice.solution: Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments = 12,00,000 − 9,00,000 = **₹3,00,000 crore**. Option (a) wrongly adds the two; (c) and (d) merely repeat given numbers.
practice.shortcut: Primary = fiscal minus interest — subtract, never add.

practice.q: India's new series of national accounts (GDP) released on 27 February 2026 has which base year?
practice.solution: MoSPI released the **GDP series with base year 2022-23** on 27 February 2026 (replacing 2011-12), with a far larger deflator set. IIP followed the same base from 1 June 2026; CPI uses calendar year 2024.
practice.shortcut: New GDP/IIP base = 2022-23; new CPI base = 2024.

practice.q: Which statement about the GST Council is correct?
options: It is chaired by the Prime Minister
States together carry one-third of the voting weight
Decisions require a two-thirds special majority of members present
Decisions are taken by a three-fourths weighted majority, with the Centre holding one-third weight
practice.solution: Under Art. 279A the Council is chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**, and every decision needs a **3/4th weighted majority — Centre 1/3, States together 2/3**; quorum is half the members.

practice.q: The revised Wholesale Price Index series released in June 2026 is characterised by:
options: inclusion of services in the headline WPI
an expanded basket of 957 items (from 697) alongside the launch of Producer Price Indices
a shift of compilation from DPIIT to NSO
practice.solution: DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser launched the WPI **2022-23 series on 15 June 2026**, expanding the basket from **697 to 957 items** and releasing new **Producer Price Indices**; WPI will run beside PPI for five years. Services remain outside headline WPI, and compilation stays with DPIIT.
practice.shortcut: Basket 697→957 and PPI twins — both changed together.

practice.q: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which becomes effective from 1 April 2026, is notable for:
options: introducing a single 'tax year' and replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961
raising the basic exemption limit to ₹7 lakh
practice.solution: The Income-tax Act, 2025 consolidates the 1961 Act into **536 sections across 23 chapters** and replaces the previous-year/assessment-year pair with one **'tax year'** (first applicable to income of FY 2026-27). Rates and slabs are essentially unchanged; GST law is untouched.
practice.shortcut: Keyword of the new Act = 'tax year' — nothing about GST or new slabs.

practice.q: Which one of the following is correct about India's Monetary Policy Committee and inflation target?
options: The MPC has 9 members and targets WPI inflation
The MPC has 6 members and targets CPI inflation of 4% with a ±2% band
The MPC has 6 members and targets CPI inflation of 5% with a ±1% band
The MPC has 4 members and the Governor has no casting vote
practice.solution: Since the RBI Act amendment of 2016, the **MPC has 6 members** (3 RBI including the Governor, who holds a casting vote, and 3 government nominees) with a flexible inflation target of **4% CPI ± 2%**.

practice.q: **National income** of India is conventionally defined as —
practice.solution: Textbook national income = **Net National Product at factor cost** — GNP minus depreciation, adjusted for indirect taxes and subsidies.

practice.q: Which one of the following is **correct**?
practice.solution: **GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad.** The other relations invert or misuse the links: NNP = GNP − depreciation; GDP ignores NFIA.
practice.shortcut: GNP starts from GDP and adds NFIA.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Depreciation is deducted while moving from GNP to NNP.
2. Indirect taxes are subtracted while moving from market prices to factor cost.
3. GDP includes net factor income from abroad.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — **GNP**, not GDP, brings in net factor income from abroad.

practice.q: GDP measured at **constant prices** is called —
practice.solution: **Real GDP** values output at base-year prices, stripping out inflation. Nominal (current-price) GDP mixes price and volume changes.

practice.q: If the GDP deflator is 125 and nominal GDP is ₹500 lakh crore, **real GDP** is —
practice.solution: Real GDP = Nominal ÷ (deflator ÷ 100) = 500 ÷ 1.25 = **₹400 lakh crore**. A deflator of 125 means prices are 25% above the base year.

practice.q: Nominal GDP rose 12% in a year while the deflator rose 8%. **Real growth** was approximately —
practice.solution: Real growth ≈ nominal growth − inflation measured by the deflator = 12 − 8 = **about 4%**. (Exactly: 1.12/1.08 − 1 = 3.7%.)
practice.shortcut: Subtract the deflator rise from nominal growth.

practice.q: The new series of India's national accounts released in **February 2026** uses which **base year**?
practice.solution: MoSPI released the GDP series with **base year 2022-23** in February 2026, replacing the 2011-12 base; the IIP moved to the same base from June 2026.

practice.q: The **CSO and NSSO** were merged in 2019 to form —
practice.solution: The merger created the **NSO**, which works under MoSPI and releases GDP, CPI and survey data.

practice.q: **Per capita income** is obtained by dividing —
options: GNP by the number of taxpayers
practice.solution: Per capita income = **national income ÷ population**. Using GDP or taxpayers would give different, non-standard measures.

practice.q: Which of the following is included under the **income method** of measuring national income?
practice.solution: The income method sums **factor incomes** — wages (labour), rent (land), interest (capital) and profit (enterprise). Expenditure and output methods take the other two routes to the same total.

practice.q: **Gross Value Added (GVA)** in India's national accounts is measured at —
practice.solution: India reports sectoral GVA at **basic prices**; GDP = GVA + product taxes − product subsidies. Market prices sit one step further up.
practice.shortcut: GVA = basic prices; GDP = GVA + product taxes − subsidies.

practice.q: Which of the following belongs to the **secondary sector**?
practice.solution: **Construction** is secondary (it transforms materials). Mining and fishing are primary; banking is tertiary.

practice.q: The **First Five Year Plan** (1951-56) was based on the —
practice.solution: The 1st plan used the **Harrod-Domar** growth model and gave top priority to agriculture and irrigation — a success thanks to good monsoons.

practice.q: The strategy of heavy industry and capital goods was the hallmark of the —
practice.solution: The **2nd plan (1956-61)** followed **P.C. Mahalanobis's** model — public investment in machine-building and basic industries.

practice.q: The 'Gadgil strategy' is associated with which Five Year Plan?
practice.solution: The **3rd plan (1961-66)** is linked to **D.R. Gadgil's** strategy of self-reliant growth; it was upset by the 1962 and 1965 wars and droughts, leading to the Plan Holiday.

practice.q: Which was the **last Five Year Plan** of India?
practice.solution: The **12th plan (2012-17)** — 'faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth' — was the final plan; from 2017 NITI Aayog's multi-year documents replaced plans.
practice.shortcut: 12 = the end of the plan era.

practice.q: The Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) is remembered for —
practice.solution: The **8th plan** ran with the **1991 New Economic Policy** — liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation (LPG). It began two years late after annual plans in 1990-92.

practice.q:
Arrange chronologically:
1. Plan Holiday 2. Rolling plan 3. Twelfth plan 4. Eleventh plan
practice.solution: Plan Holiday (1966-69) → Rolling plan (1978-80) → 11th plan (2007-12) → 12th plan (2012-17).

practice.q: **NITI Aayog** was established on —
practice.solution: NITI Aayog began on **1 January 2015** by a Cabinet resolution, replacing the Planning Commission created on 15 March 1950.

practice.q: Who is the **chairman** of NITI Aayog?
practice.solution: The **Prime Minister chairs** NITI Aayog. A Vice-Chairperson leads the think-tank work and a CEO (Secretaries-level officer) administers it.

practice.q:
Consider the statements about NITI Aayog:
1. It allocates plan funds to states.
2. Its Governing Council includes all Chief Ministers.
3. It has produced a 3-year action agenda.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statement 1 is wrong — NITI Aayog is **advisory** and does not allocate plan funds. Its Governing Council unites CMs and UT Lt Governors, and its planning documents include the 3-year action agenda.
practice.shortcut: NITI advises; it does not fund.

practice.q: Which one of the following pairs is **correctly matched**?
practice.solution: Both institutions were born of **Cabinet resolutions** (1950 and 2015) — neither statute nor Constitution created them. The Finance Commission, by contrast, is constitutional.

practice.q: The **Aspirational Districts Programme** is run by —
practice.solution: NITI Aayog launched the programme in **2018** covering **112** backward districts, nudging them on health, nutrition, education and infrastructure through real-time monitoring.

practice.q: The **rolling plan** concept was in operation during —
practice.solution: The **rolling plan (1978-80)** revised targets annually with a moving horizon — the concept is associated with **D.T. Lakdawala**. 1966-69 is the Plan Holiday.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Fifth Plan was terminated before its full term.
2. Annual plans were also used in 1990-92.
3. The Plan Holiday followed the Second Plan.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — the 5th plan was cut short in 1978 and annual plans ran in 1990-92. Statement 3 is wrong: the Plan Holiday followed the **Third** plan (1966-69).

practice.q: The Reserve Bank of India was **nationalised** on —
practice.solution: The RBI, created under the RBI Act 1934 and operational from 1 April 1935, was **nationalised on 1 January 1949** — ownership moved from private shareholders to the government.

practice.q: The headquarters of the RBI moved to **Mumbai** in —
practice.solution: The RBI opened in **Calcutta** in 1935 and shifted permanently to **Mumbai in 1937**.
practice.shortcut: Two years in Kolkata, then Mumbai.

practice.q: Which of the following is **not** issued by the Reserve Bank of India?
practice.solution: The **₹1 note** (and all coins) are issued by the **Government of India**; the RBI issues the rest of the currency.

practice.q: The **repo rate** is the rate at which —
options: The RBI lends short-term funds to banks
practice.solution: **Repo** = the RBI repurchases-securities rate — it lends to banks against government securities; that is why it is the main **policy rate**. The reverse direction (banks park funds) is the SDF.

practice.q: The **Bank Rate** in India's current framework is kept equal to —
practice.solution: The **Bank Rate** sits at the **MSF** level — repo **+ 25 basis points** — at the corridor ceiling; the SDF (repo − 25 bp) marks the floor.

practice.q: Arrange the rates for a given repo rate r (highest first):
practice.solution: The corridor is **SDF (r − 25 bp) < repo (r) < MSF (r + 25 bp)**. The ceiling is the MSF/bank rate; the floor is the collateral-free SDF.

practice.q: The **Monetary Policy Committee** has how many members?
practice.solution: The **six-member MPC** (RBI Act amendment, 2016) has three RBI members — including the Governor, who holds the casting vote — and three government-appointed external members.

practice.q: India's **inflation target** for monetary policy is —
practice.solution: The flexible inflation target is **4% CPI, ±2%** — set under the 2016 framework; breaching the band for three straight quarters forces a written report to the government.

practice.q: If inflation breaches the target band for **three consecutive quarters**, the RBI must —
options: Submit a written report to the government
practice.solution: The framework's failure clause: three consecutive quarters outside the 4 ± 2% band obliges the MPC majority and the Governor to **report to the government** the reasons, remedies and the time frame for return.

practice.q: Which statement about **SLR** is correct?
options: It is kept as cash with the RBI
It must be maintained in liquid assets such as government securities
It earns no return for banks
It is set by the Government of India
practice.solution: **SLR** is the bank's own stock of **liquid assets** — G-secs, gold and approved securities. CRR, not SLR, is cash with the RBI; SLR holdings do earn returns; the RBI sets the ratio under the Banking Regulation Act.
practice.shortcut: SLR = securities with the bank; CRR = cash with RBI.

practice.q: To **inject liquidity** into the system, the RBI can —
practice.solution: Open-market **purchases** pay banks money and add liquidity. Sales, higher CRR, or higher rates all drain liquidity.

practice.q: **14 major commercial banks** were nationalised in —
practice.solution: On **19 July 1969** fourteen big private banks were nationalised; **six** more followed in **1980**, deepening credit reach.

practice.q: The **State Bank of India** was created in 1955 by nationalising the —
practice.solution: The **Imperial Bank of India** became SBI under the SBI Act, 1955; its state-bank subsidiaries followed in 1959 (merged back into SBI in 2017).

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Payment banks can undertake lending activities.
2. The DICGC insures bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh.
3. NPCI operates the UPI system.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statement 1 is wrong — **payment banks accept deposits and remit funds but cannot lend**. Statements 2 and 3 are correct: DICGC cover is ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank, and NPCI runs UPI, RuPay and IMPS.
practice.shortcut: Payment banks: deposits yes, loans never.

practice.q: A **continuous fall in the general price level** is called —
practice.solution: **Deflation** = prices falling on average. Disinflation is only a slowdown in positive inflation; stagflation pairs inflation with stagnant growth.

practice.q: Inflation caused by **excess aggregate demand** over available output is —
practice.solution: **Demand-pull** = 'too much money chasing too few goods' — from credit booms, tax cuts or spending surges. Input-cost shocks (crude, wages) create cost-push inflation.

practice.q: An economy shows **rising prices along with falling output and rising unemployment**. This is —
practice.solution: **Stagflation** = stagnation (weak growth, job losses) plus inflation — the classic outcome of a severe cost-push shock, as in the 1970s oil crises.

practice.q: The **CPI (Combined)** for India is released by —
practice.solution: The **National Statistical Office** (Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation) compiles CPI Combined, rural and urban series. DPIIT does the WPI; the Labour Bureau does CPI-IW/AL/RL.

practice.q: Which statement about the **WPI** is correct?
options: It measures prices at the wholesale/producer stage and covers only goods
It is compiled by the NSO
It is the RBI's inflation target
practice.solution: The WPI tracks **wholesale-stage prices of goods** — services stay out. The NSO's CPI is the retail gauge, and the RBI targets **CPI**, not WPI.

practice.q: The **Reserve Bank's inflation target** is framed on —
practice.solution: Since 2016 the nominal anchor is **headline CPI (Combined)** at 4% ± 2% — the WPI is watched but not targeted.

practice.q: The **new WPI series (2022-23 base)** launched in June 2026 —
options: Included services for the first time
Expanded the basket from 697 to 957 items and added Producer Price Indices
Replaced the CPI as the target index
practice.solution: The revised series widened the basket to **957 items** and introduced **PPIs** alongside the WPI; services remain outside the headline WPI and compilation stays with DPIIT's Office of Economic Adviser.

practice.q: Before the current revisions, the base years of **CPI and WPI** respectively were —
practice.solution: The old CPI series used calendar-year base **2012**; the old WPI used **2011-12**. The new bases are 2024 (CPI) and 2022-23 (WPI).

practice.q: **Core inflation** excludes —
practice.solution: **Core = headline − food and fuel**, filtering out volatile supply-driven swings to reveal underlying price pressure.

practice.q: Which one of the following is **correctly matched**?
practice.solution: Stagflation pairs **inflation with stagnation**. Disinflation = slower (still positive) inflation; deflation = falling prices; reflation = measures to lift prices/demand back up.

practice.q: The dearness allowance of central government employees is revised using —
practice.solution: **CPI-IW** (Industrial Workers), compiled by the **Labour Bureau**, is the DA anchor. CPI-AL/RL serve agricultural and rural labourers.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The IIP measures changes in industrial production.
2. The eight core industries include fertilisers and cement.
3. The IIP is a price index.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — the **IIP is an output index**, not a price index; the WPI/CPI track prices.

practice.q: The **fiscal deficit** is best defined as —
options: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings
practice.solution: **Fiscal deficit** = the government's total borrowing requirement for the year — total expenditure minus all receipts other than borrowings. The first option defines revenue deficit.

practice.q: Total expenditure ₹45 lakh crore; receipts excluding borrowings ₹39 lakh crore. The **fiscal deficit** equals —
practice.solution: 45 − 39 = **₹6 lakh crore** — computed as expenditure minus non-borrowed receipts.

practice.q: Fiscal deficit is ₹6 lakh crore and interest payments ₹10 lakh crore. The **primary deficit** is —
practice.solution: 6 − 10 = **−₹4 lakh crore**, i.e. a primary surplus: excluding past interest, this year's operations raise no new borrowing.
practice.shortcut: PD = FD − interest; here it flips negative.

practice.q: A government has revenue receipts ₹25, revenue expenditure ₹28 (all figures lakh crore). Its **revenue deficit** is —
practice.solution: 28 − 25 = **₹3 lakh crore** — revenue spending exceeds revenue income, so borrowing finances routine running costs.

practice.q: The **Annual Financial Statement** of the Union is laid before Parliament under —
practice.solution: **Article 112** presents estimated receipts and expenditure — the constitutional name for the Union Budget. Articles 266-267 deal with the funds; 280 is the Finance Commission.

practice.q: Which statement about the **Consolidated Fund of India** is correct?
options: No money can be withdrawn without appropriation by Parliament
Money is held in trust and needs no parliamentary approval
It is at the President's personal disposal
practice.solution: Article 266(1): every withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund needs **Parliament's authorisation**. The trust balances with no vote sit in the Public Account; the President's discretion runs on the Contingency Fund.

practice.q: **Disinvestment proceeds** of the government are classified as —
practice.solution: Selling government equity **reduces assets** — the defining mark of a capital receipt, along with borrowings and loan recoveries.

practice.q: Revenue deficit is ₹3 lakh crore, including grants of ₹1 lakh crore for creation of capital assets. The **effective revenue deficit** is —
practice.solution: ERD = RD − grants for capital assets = 3 − 1 = **₹2 lakh crore** — introduced in 2011-12 to show borrowing that funds only consumption.

practice.q: Which one of the following is **correct**?
options: The FRBM Act was enacted in 1991
Subsidies are the largest revenue-expenditure head
practice.solution: **Primary deficit = fiscal deficit − interest payments**, isolating this year's borrowing appetite. FRBM came in 2003; interest payments top the expenditure list; fiscal deficit is defined including the effect of borrowing needs.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The FRBM Act gives legal backing to deficit targets.
2. Interest payments are the largest single item of government expenditure.
3. Fiscal deficit can never exceed revenue deficit.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false — the fiscal deficit (total borrowing need) routinely **exceeds** the revenue deficit because capital expenditure is also financed by borrowing.
practice.shortcut: FD ≥ RD is the normal case.

practice.q: The Union Budget is presented on **1 February** since —
practice.solution: From **2017** the Budget moved to 1 February — giving ministries time to spend from April 1 — and the **Railway Budget was merged** the same year.

practice.q: Approval of government **expenditure** proceeds through —
options: The Appropriation Bill on Demands for Grants
practice.solution: Each ministry's **Demand for Grants** is voted; the **Appropriation Bill** then authorises withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund. The Finance Bill carries tax proposals instead.

practice.q: The **GST Council** was established under —
practice.solution: **Article 279A** (101st Amendment, 2016) creates the GST Council; 246A grants the taxing power and 269A handles IGST apportionment. 280 is the Finance Commission.

practice.q: In GST Council decisions, the **Union government's weighted vote share** is —
practice.solution: Decisions need a **three-fourths weighted majority**: the Centre holds **one-third** of the votes and all states together **two-thirds** — so states can block, but the Centre can also veto.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Union Finance Minister chairs the GST Council.
2. GST on inter-state supply is called IGST.
3. GST Council decisions are binding recommendations implemented by law.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: All three are correct — the Union FM chairs, inter-state supply attracts IGST (Article 269A), and Council recommendations are implemented through changes in GST laws.
practice.shortcut: Chair, IGST, binding recommendations — all true.

practice.q: Goods and Services Tax was introduced in India from —
practice.solution: GST rolled out on **1 July 2017** under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** — a destination-based tax subsuming excise, service tax, VAT and a host of cesses.

practice.q: Under the **GST 2.0** structure effective 22 September 2025, which slab was **abolished**?
practice.solution: The reform kept **5% (merit)** and **18% (standard)**, added a **40% demerit rate** (tobacco, pan masala, certain luxury goods) and **abolished the 12% slab**, with the 28% rate retired into the demerit track.

practice.q: An intra-state sale under GST attracts —
practice.solution: Intra-state supply splits between **CGST** (Centre) and **SGST** (state); **IGST** applies only to inter-state supplies and imports.

practice.q: Which of the following is an **indirect tax**?
practice.solution: **Customs duty** is loaded onto import prices and borne by consumers — indirect. Corporate tax, STT and capital-gains tax fall on the taxpayer directly.

practice.q: The burden of a **direct tax** —
options: Falls on the person who pays it to the government
Is shared equally by buyers and sellers
Is borne by the next purchaser
practice.solution: A direct tax **cannot legally be shifted** — the payer suffers it. Indirect taxes are passed down the price chain to the final consumer.

practice.q: The **Income-tax Act, 2025** came into force on —
practice.solution: The new code took effect from **1 April 2026**, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961 and introducing the single '**tax year**'.

practice.q: The '**tax year**' introduced by the Income-tax Act, 2025 —
options: Replaces both previous year and assessment year
practice.solution: The 2025 Act collapses the twin concepts of 'previous year' and 'assessment year' into one '**tax year**' — a plain-language simplification across its 536 sections.

practice.q: Which of the following is **exempt from income tax** under Indian law?
practice.solution: **Agricultural income** stays outside income tax — taxing it is a state power. Salaries, HRA above limits and share capital gains are all taxable.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. GST is a destination-based consumption tax.
2. The GSTN provides the IT backbone for GST compliance.
3. Cesses and surcharges form part of the divisible pool with states.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is the classic trap — **cesses and surcharges sit outside the divisible pool**, so states do not share them under the Finance Commission's award.
practice.shortcut: Cess never reaches the shared pool.

practice.q: **Swachh Bharat Mission** was launched on —
practice.solution: Launched on **Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2014**, with rural (Grameen) and urban arms for sanitation and open-defecation-free status.

practice.q: **PM SVANidhi** scheme provides collateral-free working-capital loans to —
practice.solution: **PM SVANidhi (2020)**, run by MoHUA, gives street vendors working-capital loans with digital-repayment incentives.

practice.q: **PM Gati Shakti** — the national master plan for multi-modal infrastructure — was launched in —
practice.solution: Launched **October 2021**, it stitches ministries onto one GIS platform for integrated infrastructure planning.

practice.q: Under **PM-KISAN**, each eligible landholding farmer family receives —
practice.solution: **₹6,000 a year in three DBT instalments** (₹2,000 each), launched February 2019.

practice.q: The **₹5 lakh per family per year** hospitalisation cover is provided under —
practice.solution: **PM-JAY (23 September 2018)** covers secondary and tertiary hospitalisation up to ₹5 lakh a family a year; PMJJBY is a life-insurance scheme.

practice.q: Match: 1. PM-KISAN 2. PM-JAY 3. MUDRA — with (i) 2019 (ii) 2018 (iii) 2015:
practice.solution: PM-KISAN **2019**; PM-JAY **2018**; MUDRA **2015** — the standard launch-year trio.

practice.q: The **VB-G RAM G** scheme, effective 1 July 2026, guarantees —
practice.solution: It replaced MGNREGA's 100-day guarantee with **125 days per rural household per year**, paying wages **weekly**.

practice.q: **DAY-NRLM** promotes rural livelihoods mainly through —
practice.solution: The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (2011) organises rural poor women into **SHGs** for credit access and enterprise; its urban twin is DAY-NULM.

practice.q: Zero-balance bank accounts with a RuPay card and overdraft facility are provided under —
practice.solution: **PM Jan Dhan Yojana** (28 August 2014) is the financial-inclusion flagship — accounts, RuPay debit card, accident cover and an overdraft window.

practice.q: In **MUDRA** loans, the 'Kishor' category covers loans of —
practice.solution: MUDRA tiers: **Shishu** ≤ ₹50,000; **Kishor** ₹50,000-5 lakh; **Tarun** ₹5-10 lakh — all collateral-free micro-credit.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. Payment banks can issue credit cards.
2. PMSBY offers ₹2 lakh accidental-death cover for a ₹20 annual premium.
3. Atal Pension Yojana targets workers aged 18-40.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statement 1 is wrong — **payment banks cannot lend or issue credit cards**; statements 2 and 3 describe PMSBY and APY correctly.
practice.shortcut: Payment banks save; they don't lend.

practice.q: '**Har Ghar Jal**' (functional tap connection to every rural home) is the goal of —
practice.solution: **Jal Jeevan Mission (August 2019)**, under Jal Shakti, targets piped tap water for all rural households.

practice.q: Free **LPG connections** to women of poor households are given under —
practice.solution: **Ujjwala (1 May 2016)** hands LPG connections to women from poor families, cutting indoor smoke; Saubhagya instead electrifies households.

practice.q:
Consider the statements:
1. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission provides digital health IDs (ABHA).
2. PM Awas Yojana has separate urban and rural arms.
3. POSHAN Abhiyaan is implemented by the Ministry of Health.
Which are correct?
practice.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong — **POSHAN Abhiyaan (2018)** runs under the **Ministry of Women and Child Development**, anchored in the ICDS network.
practice.shortcut: POSHAN lives in the WCD ministry.

practice.q: **SEBI** was given statutory status by an Act of Parliament in —
practice.solution: Set up in **1988** as an executive body, SEBI became statutory under the **SEBI Act, 1992** — the Harshad Mehta scam year accelerated the change.

practice.q: The regulation of the **insurance sector** in India rests with —
practice.solution: The **Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India** (IRDA Act, 1999) polices insurers and policy-holders; headquartered at **Hyderabad**.

practice.q: Match the regulator to its market: 1. SEBI 2. IRDAI 3. PFRDA — with (i) pensions (ii) securities (iii) insurance:
practice.solution: SEBI → **securities**; IRDAI → **insurance**; PFRDA → **pensions** (it administers the NPS and Atal Pension Yojana).

practice.q: **SIDBI** is headquartered in —
practice.solution: **SIDBI (1990)** sits at **Lucknow** — the odd-one-out HQ among Indian financial institutions, and a repeated exam answer.

practice.q: The **IRDAI** is headquartered at —
practice.solution: The insurance regulator's headquarters is **Hyderabad**; SEBI and NABARD sit in Mumbai.

practice.q: **NABARD's** headquarters is located in —
practice.solution: **NABARD (1982)** is headquartered in **Mumbai**, like the RBI and SEBI; it was spun out of the RBI's agricultural refinance function.
practice.shortcut: NABARD with the RBI in Mumbai.

practice.q: **NABARD** was established in —
practice.solution: NABARD came up on **12 July 1982**, on the Shivaraman committee's recommendation, taking over the RBI's agricultural-refinance wing.

practice.q: Which pair is **correctly matched**?
practice.solution: **SIDBI — 1990** is correct. EXIM Bank is 1982; NHB 1988; NABARD 1982.

practice.q: The **Asian Development Bank (ADB)** is headquartered in —
practice.solution: The **ADB (1966)** sits at **Manila**, Philippines — the standard HQ question on regional banks.

practice.q: The **New Development Bank**, set up by the BRICS countries, is headquartered in —
practice.solution: The **NDB (2015)** works from **Shanghai** with **K.V. Kamath** as first president; the AIIB (2016) sits separately in Beijing.

practice.q: The **Sensex** is an index of —
practice.solution: **Sensex = 30 BSE stocks** (free-float weighted); the NSE's counterpart is the **Nifty 50**.

practice.q: Which of the following is **correctly matched**?
practice.solution: **RuPay** is NPCI's domestic card network. UPI belongs to NPCI, not SEBI; Nifty is the **NSE's** index; FASTag is a road-toll payment tag.
